PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL - ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION / ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
MEMORANDUM (esg-gap-analysis-memo.docx content)
To: Patricia Huang, General Counsel, Greenfield Consumer Products Inc. | From: Aldridge & Whitmore LLP ESG Practice | Re: Gap analysis, Draft FY2024 ESG Report (3/10/2025)

1. BOTTOM LINE
The draft should not be published as written. Five findings carry securities-law exposure (Critical): (1) net-zero claim contradicting the Board resolution; (2) Scope 3 misstatement; (3) false "100%" vulnerability-assessment claim; (4) SBTi "aligned" language; (5) unreliable Scope 2 build-up. Each is contradicted by Greenfield's own records, which supports scienter arguments. Hargrave & Fenton should be engaged now.

2. LEGAL BASELINE (corrects the checklist and instructions)
SEC. The 2024 climate rules (Rel. 33-11275; 17 CFR 229.1500-1508) are stayed; on 3/27/2025 the SEC voted to stop defending them and the Eighth Circuit (Iowa v. SEC) has held the case in abeyance since 2025 (motion to lift denied 5/21/2026, per secondary sources). They are not "proposed" and are not reinstated. They also do not do what the checklist says: Scope 1/2 is required only if material, there is no mandatory Scope 3, no mandatory location/market dual reporting, no director climate-expertise or ESG-pay disclosure (dropped from the proposal), and scenario analysis, carbon price and targets are required only if used/material. Large accelerated filer GHG disclosure was FY2026 with limited assurance FY2029. Practical exposure comes from antifraud law: Rule 10b-5 / Exchange Act 10(b), Securities Act 11/12(a)(2) (only if the report is incorporated into a registration statement, e.g., S-3/S-8 - verify), Rule 14a-9 if tied to the proxy, SEC 2010 climate guidance (Rel. 33-9106), and SEC ESG enforcement (e.g., DWS 2023; Keurig Dr Pepper 2024). Macquarie v. Moab (2024): pure omissions are not 10b-5(b) claims, but half-truths are; Omnicare (2015) governs opinions. The PSLRA safe harbor does not cover statements of present or historical fact (items 1-4 below), and boilerplate disclaimers do not cure known contrary facts. I benchmark to the stayed rule as the Board asked, but rate severity by antifraud risk, not by the checklist's overstated requirements.
California. SB 253 (Health & Safety Code 38532) and SB 261 (38533) apply to the parent as an entity "doing business in California" (>$1B and >$500M revenue); Greenfield West's revenue is not the test, and the parent's $8.7B qualifies. The instructions' timeline is off by a year: under CARB's 12/2024 enforcement notice and SB 219, first Scope 1/2 reports in 2026 (CARB-proposed deadline 8/10/2026) cover FY2025 data; Scope 3 begins 2027 on FY2026 data; limited assurance for Scope 1/2 starts 2026, reasonable 2030. SB 261: on 11/18/2025 the Ninth Circuit enjoined enforcement pending appeal, so the 1/1/2026 date is not currently enforceable; appeal outcome after argument (1/9/2026) is not confirmed here and must be rechecked. SB 261 requires TCFD/ISSB-aligned reporting (or an explanation of gaps) - it does not itself mandate quantified scenarios or specific temperature pathways, contrary to the checklist. SB 253 does not state a 15-category test; the GHG Protocol Scope 3 Standard requires listing excluded categories with justification. Also relevant: California AB 1305 (Health & Safety Code 44475 et seq.), which requires website substantiation (basis, interim progress, third-party verification) for net-zero/"significant reduction" claims by entities operating in California - not in the checklist; confirm applicability.
EU. The checklist is outdated. Directive (EU) 2025/794 postponed "wave 2" (large non-PIE companies like Greenfield Europe GmbH) by two years: FY2027, reporting 2028, not FY2025. The Omnibus I amendments (effective 3/2026 per secondary sources) raise scope to >1,000 employees AND >EUR 450M turnover, and for non-EU parents require >EUR 450M EU turnover plus an EU subsidiary/branch >EUR 200M (EUR 780M and EUR 620M: met), first report FY2028 (2029). Simplified ESRS were slated for adoption in 2026 - verify. The EUR 150M parent threshold in the checklist is superseded. Employee count conflict: the report says 8,500 EU employees; instructions/checklist say about 4,100; the GmbH must confirm its own headcount for the 1,000 test. German transposition status needs local-counsel confirmation. CSDDD, as narrowed (about 5,000 employees / EUR 1.5B), likely does not reach Greenfield (EU turnover EUR 780M) - the checklist's contrary statement should be withdrawn. ESRS 1 allows first-year comparative relief; the FY2024 report need not be ESRS-compliant.

3. FINDINGS (severity | issue | authority | evidence | fix)
C1 CRITICAL. Net-zero overstated. Report (CEO letter; Goals table; s.4.1) says net-zero across all scopes by 2040. Board Resolution 9/15/2024 s.III.B: net-zero for Scope 1 and 2 only, by 2045; s.IV.C: no Scope 3 net-zero adopted; s.IV.E forbids implying one; s.V.C directs the GC to ensure accuracy. Authority: Rule 10b-5; AB 1305; FTC Green Guides (if marketing). Fix: restate as "Scope 1 and 2 net-zero by 2045 (90% absolute reduction, residual <=10%); Scope 3 interim target submitted to SBTi; Board to consider long-term Scope 3 by Q2 2025."
C2 CRITICAL. Scope 3 internally inconsistent. Report states 3,640,000 (13.3% reduction; total 4,266,000) but its own category table sums to 3,840,000 and the workbook shows 3,840,000 (8.6%; total 4,466,000). The Goals table says 8.6%. Overstates progress by 4.7 points and understates emissions by 200,000 mtCO2e (5.2%). Comp Committee minutes (Vasquez: ~3.8M) show management knew. Authority: 10b-5; GHG Protocol. Fix: 3,840,000 / 8.6% / 4,466,000 throughout; Scope 3 share 86%.
C3 CRITICAL. Vulnerability assessments. Report (s.6.2): "100% of 23 facilities completed." Tracker (updated 3/5/2025, five days before the draft): 19/23 (82.6%); Southeast Asia 0/3, Gdansk not started; $900M (22.8%) of assets unassessed. The $1.2B high-risk table includes unassessed Ho Chi Minh City and Gdansk and omits Houston ($210M, rated High); the tracker cannot reconcile $1.2B (completed High $980M plus the two unassessed zones = $1.41B). Fix: state 19 of 23, by region, with revised dates; rebuild the exposure table by rating, with unassessed sites separately.
C4 CRITICAL. SBTi. Report says targets are "aligned with SBTi" and "consistent with the SBTi's criteria for well-below 2C." SBTi (7/22 and 11/13/2024) says targets are not validated, forbids "aligned," allows "submitted/committed," and flags Scope 3 screening and emission-factor questions; validation due Q2 2025. "Well-below 2C" is also stale (SBTi near-term criteria require 1.5C for Scope 1/2). Board's Scope 1/2-only net-zero is in tension with the SBTi Net-Zero Standard, which requires Scope 3 coverage. Fix: use SBTi's approved phrasing; disclose pending status and risk of non-validation; do not describe "1.5C/Paris-aligned" until validated.
C5 CRITICAL. Scope 2 integrity. (a) Report omits location-based 289,000 despite workbook/Ridgeway dual reporting. (b) Workbook totals do not foot: facility lines sum to 341,695 (location) and 262,305 (market) versus 289,000/214,000 labeled "adjusted for rounding" (gaps of 52,695 and 48,305). If market-based is 262,305, Scope 1+2 is 674,305 and the reduction is 16.5%, not 22.5%. Ridgeway says it tested mathematical accuracy; this undermines reliance. (c) RECs described in mtCO2e; instruments are MWh (252,000 MWh applied); Frankfurt shown as GO-covered while report cites a wind PPA. (d) Workbook includes Jakarta and Rotterdam sites outside the 23-facility/country list, and 2023 Scope 1 differs between tabs (425,940 vs 438,000). Fix: Apex to reconcile and re-issue; notify Ridgeway before any assurance reference is repeated; disclose both methods.
H1 HIGH. Assurance language. "Verified" overstates limited assurance; Appendix B omits that location-based Scope 2 was covered, cites ISAE 3000/3410 but the letter also cites AICPA AT-C 210, and says the base year/prior years were not assured (first engagement); report should say so. Ridgeway is also the financial auditor: confirm Audit Committee pre-approval and SEC independence compliance (Reg S-X 2-01); obtain Ridgeway's consent to the summary and use outside the letter's restriction.
H2 HIGH. Scope 3 completeness and method. Report says it "evaluated the fifteen categories" and reports the material ones; workbook says no screening was done and 10 categories lack justification (including 2, 3, 6, 7, 9, 10). Method labels are wrong (Cat 4 is a hybrid, Cat 11 uses Apex proprietary modeling, Cat 12 uses EPA WARM); +/-20% uncertainty is not disclosed. Fix: perform and disclose a screening before publication, or say none was performed; correct labels and uncertainty.
H3 HIGH. Scenario analysis. Qualitative only, no named pathways, time horizons, or financial effects, although $1.2B exposure and $340M high-carbon revenue are identified. Not mandated by the stayed SEC rule or SB 261 text, but expected under TCFD/ISSB (SB 261), ESRS E1-9 and by Director Okafor. Fix: describe horizons; add at least 1.5C and high-warming scenarios; quantify or state why not; plan for SB 261 report.
H4 HIGH. Governance accuracy. Report: 8 directors (3 women); Board resolution lists 9 directors present. Report: Compensation Committee of four; minutes show three members. Report lists a 11/14 meeting; minutes say the next meeting was 11/7. Minutes show STIP is 100% financial and ESG pay metrics were deferred (proposal due March 2025); the report is silent - state that no ESG metrics are in incentives. Northbridge is described as the Committee's independent consultant and as financial advisor to the company: assess independence/disclosure (Reg S-K 407(e)(3)(iv); NYSE 303A.05). Minutes also misname Aldridge & Whitmore as external auditor - correct. No director climate-competency disclosure (not required by the final SEC rule; required by ESRS GOV-1).
M1 MEDIUM. ESRS readiness: no double materiality assessment (ESRS 1, IRO-1/2), E1-5 energy consumption and mix absent (GRI 302-1 marked "partial"), E1-9 financial effects, E1-8 (state no internal price), E2 pollution absent, E3-4 water consumption/discharge/stress absent (withdrawal only), E5 disposal-method split absent (39% hazardous waste unexplained), S1 gaps (TRIR methodology, contractors, pay metrics), S2 (Tier 1 only), G1 absent. Build gap register and roadmap; do not overstate in report.
M2 MEDIUM. Smaller items: emissions intensity (72.0 mtCO2e/$M, workbook) omitted; 22% fleet electrification, 85,000 MWh savings, 45% recycled content, and 100% Tier 1 "by spend" metrics lack support in the data room.

4. INTERNAL CONSISTENCY SUMMARY
Report vs source: Scope 3 (workbook); net-zero (resolution); 100% (tracker); SBTi (emails); Scope 2 (workbook, letter); board/committee composition (resolution, minutes); assurance wording (letter); EU headcount (8,500 vs 4,100). Matches: Scope 1 412,000 and components; baseline 808,000; EUR/USD conversions; 15.4% and 3.9% ratios; Ridgeway engagement number.

5. SECURITIES-LAW DISCUSSION (C1-C5)
Materiality (Basic v. Levinson): Greenfield's investors and analysts focus on climate; the Board itself ordered accuracy, tracking and targets, so they are important. Falsity is established by Greenfield's own documents. Scienter risk is elevated: the tracker, the workbook (200,000 mt difference) and the resolution were in hand before 3/10/2025, SBTi guidance was copied to the GC, and the Board expressly directed review (Res. s.V.C). Safe harbor is unavailable for present facts. Section 11 depends on incorporation into a registration statement; Rule 14a-9 on proxy linkage; Delaware oversight (Caremark) risk rises if known issues go unremedied. Recommend: Audit/Sustainability Committee sign-off, a documented review file, and consideration of whether corrective disclosure is needed if any version has already been distributed.

6. REMEDIATION ROADMAP
Before publication (by 4/30/2025, hold release if unresolved): P1 fix C1-C4 text (days 1-5; Legal/Sustainability); P1 Apex reconciliation of Scope 2 and Scope 3, Ridgeway notice (by 4/18); P1 H1 assurance wording, consent, independence check; P1 Hargrave & Fenton coordination on 10-K/proxy consistency and S-3/S-8 incorporation; P2 H4 governance corrections and ESG-pay statement; P2 H2 screening or disclosure of its absence; P2 H3 horizons/named scenarios; complete tracker or disclose revised dates; Committee approval.
By Q2 2025: Board Scope 3 recommendation (Res. s.IV.D); SBTi response and status update (30 business days from any request); Comp Committee proposal.
Through 2026: SB 253 first-cycle Scope 1/2 filing (FY2025 data) and assurance readiness, Scope 3 on FY2026 data in 2027; SB 261 report plan and monitor Ninth Circuit; double materiality and ESRS gap register for Greenfield Europe GmbH (FY2027 start unless law changes; parent FY2028); Gdansk and Southeast Asia assessments finished; reassess everything against the final SEC position and simplified ESRS.

7. LIMITS
Secondary sources supported post-2025 developments; confirm primary texts, the Ninth Circuit outcome, German transposition and final ESRS before relying.
